ar_p_k_boulder.blurb: P.K. Boulder is a single block in the small Fern climbing area of northwest Arkansas. From the parking area you walk west up to the cliff top, then scramble down around the north side of the block. It holds eight lines, six of them sport and two trad, running from 5.7 up to one 5.11. Four sit in the 5.10 range and three are 5.7 or 5.8, so it suits a mixed group. Fern as a whole is compact: a creek runs through it and most of its climbs stay under 50 feet. The same walk-in also leads to several neighboring boulders.

ar_honeycomb_wall.blurb: Honeycomb Wall is a sport wall within Rock Creek, a steep, backwoods crag in north-central Arkansas. It has eight bolted routes, and the grades lean hard: one at 5.8, one at 5.10, five at 5.11 and a single 5.12. That makes it a better stop for climbers working the middle of the 5.11 range than for beginners. To find it, follow the way to Spivey Wall, then keep going left along the base of the cliff for about five minutes. Rock Creek overall has a band of cliff 50 to 80 feet tall, where drop knees and kneebars come in handy.

ar_creek_bed.blurb: Creek Bed is a small boulder sector at Mossy Bluff, a public park inside Heber Springs, Arkansas. It has eight problems, ranging from V3 to V9: one V3, one V4, three V5, two V8 and a V9, so there is a gap between the mid-grade lines and the hard ones. At least one line begins underneath a roof. Mossy Bluff as a whole is a local bouldering spot rather than a destination, and rock quality swings from soft and sandy in places to very hard. Light traffic means holds and topouts collect dirt, moss and leaves, so bring a brush.

ar_honeycomb_boulder.blurb: Honeycomb Boulder sits in the North Forty Boulders on the north side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas. Walk up the main trail toward the Northy Forties and it appears on your left. The boulder carries eight problems, mostly easy to moderate: three at V2, then a V3, two V4s, a V5 and a V6 traverse across the front face. The face is covered in incut holds, which gives the lines a pleasant, textured feel. They are not considered the ranch's big classics, but they move well and make a handy stop on a North Forty circuit.

ar_bigfoot_proper.blurb: Bigfoot Proper is the main hollow that gives the Bigfoot Hollow area its name, in the eastern Boston Mountains near Ozark, about an hour from Fayetteville. A cliff of roughly 90 feet, a pile of boulders and a waterfall that flows seasonally define the spot. It has eight climbs: six boulder problems from V3 to V7, plus two sport routes at 5.8 and 5.10. One of the sport lines is a 70-foot arete that works as a warm-up for the harder wall nearby. The hollow is reached from Shores Lake Road by following an old road to the creek and then heading uphill. Rock quality across the wider area varies.

ar_propagation_panel.blurb: Propagation Panel is a wall of short, powerful sport climbs in The Garden at Cowell, in the Cowell and Deer area of north-central Arkansas. It is the first developed wall you meet on the way in: go around the left corner of the cliff line, squeeze between the face and some big boulders, then bear left uphill. Of its eight routes, seven are bolted and one is trad. The grades start at 5.10 with five at 5.11 and two at 5.12, so it is aimed at climbers already comfortable on steep, hard sport. Routes are around 35 feet tall and tend to go through bulges.

ar_spooky_dooky_wall.blurb: Spooky Dooky Wall is a short, shady, east-facing crag on the west side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas. Two distinct faces make it up. On the left, lines start from a ledge and head up a clean grey face with few features and a slight overhang. On the right, the rock is sculpted into jugs and ripples. Seven of the eight routes are sport and one is trad, with grades from 5.7 to 5.11: one at 5.7, three at 5.8, one at 5.9, two at 5.10 and one 5.11. Routes run around 30 feet, and a stick clip is recommended.
